text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.
- President Franjo Tudjman is expected to announce his candidacy at the next presidential election on Sunday, March 23.
- Interpol barges into the homes of three underaged hackers from Zadar who may have broken into the Pentagon database while surfing the Internet.
- Croatia hopes to join the World Trade Organisation (WTO) but needs time to adapt its laws to the newly liberalised telecoms regulations, says Economy Ministry official Olga Spevec.
- Public health general practitioners may be required to extend their working hours to be at patients' disposal between 7 a.m. and 9 p.m.
- Agriculture Ministry hopes to help farmers finance spring sowings by granting them loans of 2,500 kuna for each heifers.

- Interview with new Privatisation Fund president Tomislav Druzak: Food firm Belje will be the first company from Serb-held Eastern Slavonia to be taken over. Kras and EBRD soon to sign an agreement on investment.
- Commentary: Croatia is mounting diplomatic warfare to be included in the main European road corridors.

- Bina Istra, a joint venture of French firm Bouygues, INA and Istarska Autocesta, is to launch a 12.5 million kuna share issue to raise capital for building a motorway through the tourist Istrian peninsula. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
